## SECTION 0 — HOW TO READ THIS ANALYSIS

**Valuation engine selected:** Free Cash Flow to the Firm (FCFF) discounted at WACC, net debt subtracted. I use FCFF rather than FCFE because RingCentral is deliberately deleveraging (gross debt target $1B by end-2026, no maturities until 2030) and FCFF avoids modelling the financing decision separately. SBC is treated as a real expense per the pack instruction — an owner-earnings figure that starts from OCF and does not subtract SBC is overstated.

**Data hierarchy:** Filed SEC numbers > arithmetic on filed numbers > company guidance in press releases > third-party aggregator estimates > my labelled assumptions. The pack's SEC-extracted figures are authoritative for historical financials. The company's own press releases define FCF differently from the pack's `capex` column (pack capex is PP&E-only; company FCF subtracts PP&E *plus* capitalized software). I use the company's broader capex definition for forecasting because it matches guided FCF.

## SECTION 8 — VALUATION ENGINE & DISCOUNT-RATE DERIVATION

**Engine selection.** I use a **10-year, two-stage equity-levered owner-earnings DCF** — discounting (FCF − SBC), which is cash-to-equity after interest, at the **cost of equity**, then subtracting net debt and adding back cash (equivalently: *subtract net debt*). I chose this over a WACC/FCFF engine because: (1) the pack's own guidance — SBC is a real cost; (2) OCF is already after-interest so levered FCFE is the natural unit; (3) the company has negative book equity, making capital-structure-weights-based WACC fragile; (4) it avoids fabricating a tax rate the pack withholds. The net-debt subtraction is correct here because the convertibles are out-of-the-money (pure debt, repaid in cash) and management is demonstrably deleveraging — I take no credit for the interest savings the repayment creates (flat OCF margin), which offsets the face-value-vs-discounted timing of the deduction and keeps the base case conservative.

## SECTION 12 — FINAL EXECUTION OPINION

**Intrinsic value.** Base case **~$67/share** (owner-earnings DCF: 10% cost of equity, 2.5% terminal growth, net debt $1.12B, SBC expensed in full). Sensible parameter range **$55–85**; full scenario range **$36 (bear) – $102 (bull)**.

**Against a price of $66.47, the margin of safety is approximately zero.** The stock's 175% re-rating off the 52-week low has fully priced the FCF inflection and the SBC-reduction plan — indeed it prices the plan at its *most likely* outcome with no cushion for the obvious failure modes (Microsoft share pressure, SBC compression stalling, growth fading below 3%). The market is paying ~18.7x 2026 owner earnings for a ~5%-grower; that is fair-to-full, not cheap.

**Execution stance:** **HOLD — do not initiate at $66.47, do not chase.** 
- **Accumulation zone:** below **~$50–55** (≈ 20–30% margin of safety against base; ≈ the sell-side mean, and where the bear case is already roughly paid for).
- **Clear sell/avoid zone:** above **~$75–80** (requires bull-case outcomes to be right).
- **Positioning discipline:** given 17.7% short interest and a binary AI-monetization set-up, this is not a size-able position either way at fair value; if you hold, treat the dividend ($0.50/yr, ~0.75% yield) and buyback as the only compensation for carrying a 10%-discount-rate risk at a zero-margin-of-safety price.
- **Trigger to re-rate the thesis upward:** evidence the SBC glide to 4% is on track *and* AI-driven ARR re-accelerates revenue toward 6–7% — that combination would push fair value into the $80–100 zone.
- **Trigger to cut:** revenue growth <3% for two consecutive quarters, or SBC compression stalling, or a Microsoft-led UCaaS pricing/attrition event.

**Bottom line.** RingCentral is a genuinely improved business — deleveraging, 23–27% FCF margins, market-leading UCaaS share, an AI attach doubling YoY — but **at $66.47 the market and I agree on its value, and agreement with the market is not a thesis.** I would be a buyer with a margin of safety, not at the current quote; the expected return at T0 is approximately the cost of equity, with a fat left tail.

**Verdict: FAIRLY VALUED / HOLD at $66.47. Intrinsic value ≈ $67 (range $55–85). No margin of safety. Accumulate < $50–55.**
